citeAs: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang (2025). WebWalker: Benchmarking LLMs in Web Traversal. arXiv:2501.07572.
creator: Jialong Wu, Wenbiao Yin, Yong Jiang, Zhenglin Wang, Zekun Xi, Runnan Fang, Linhai Zhang, Yulan He, Deyu Zhou, Pengjun Xie, Fei Huang (Tongyi Lab, Alibaba Group)
description: WebWalkerQA is a benchmark designed to assess the ability of LLMs to perform web traversal, evaluating their capacity to traverse a website's subpages to extract high-quality data systematically. It comprises 680 question-answer pairs from four real-world domains (conference, organization, education, and game) across over 1373 webpages, with both single-source and multi-source QA types in English and Chinese.
name: WebWalkerQA
rai:dataAnnotationPlatform: Crowd-sourced human annotators (platform not specified); GPT-4o used for initial LLM-based annotation
rai:dataAnnotationProtocol: Two-stage funnel annotation: (1) LLM-based annotation using GPT-4o to generate synthetic QA pairs — traversing official websites recursively, constructing queries based on page information, and verifying/filtering for legitimate queries with short answers containing entities; (2) Human annotation where crowd-sourced annotators rewrite and calibrate questions and answers to ensure QA pairs are correct and consistent. Both multi-source (requiring information from multiple distinct web pages) and single-source (information from a single page) types were constructed.
rai:dataBiases: The dataset focuses on four specific domains (conference, organization, education, game) selected because they provide authoritative information and contain rich clickable content. These domains were chosen to reflect real-world scenarios with structured paths and clickable buttons. The dataset is bilingual (Chinese and English), reflecting the most widely used languages in real-world web environments, with Chinese accounting for 60.5% and English 39.5%.
rai:dataCollection: A two-stage funnel annotation strategy was employed. First, official websites were traversed recursively to collect information on accessible sub-links and their respective pages. Queries were constructed based on page information and specified roles (solo page or multiple pages simultaneously). GPT-4o performed initial annotations to generate synthetic QA pairs, followed by crowd-sourced human annotators conducting quality control and filtering. Root pages were identified through Google search using keywords such as "conference official website" or "game official website", followed by manual filtering. For the education domain, official websites of university computer science departments were chosen.
rai:dataCollectionRawData: Official websites across conference, organization, education, and game domains. The collection includes root pages and their accessible subpages, with web page content parsed into Markdown-like format using the ai4crawl tool. Pages contain clickable HTML buttons and their corresponding URLs.
rai:dataLimitations: Dataset size is limited to 680 high-quality QA pairs due to the complexity of queries in the web-agent domain. Only HTML-DOM is used to parse clickable buttons; visual modalities such as screenshots are not included. WebWalkerQA is built on official websites with dynamically updated information, while pre-trained models rely on static knowledge limited by a cutoff date. The benchmark currently only constrains actions to "click" and focuses on text-based reasoning.
rai:dataPreprocessingProtocol: Web pages were parsed into Markdown-like format using the ai4crawl tool. Clickable HTML buttons and corresponding URLs were extracted using Beautiful Soup. Synthetic QA pairs were filtered to retain only those with short answers containing entities, and queries deviating from natural, human-like phrasing were removed.
rai:dataSocialImpact: The dataset highlights the importance of deep, vertical exploration in web-based tasks, paving the way for more scalable and reliable LLM-based information retrieval integrated with RAG. It addresses the limitation of traditional search engines that perform only horizontal searches and may not effectively trace deeper content embedded within websites.
rai:dataUseCases: Benchmarking LLMs on web traversal tasks; evaluating the capacity of LLMs to traverse website subpages to extract high-quality data; assessing performance of RAG systems on deep web information retrieval; evaluating multi-agent frameworks for web navigation; supplementary training data (approximately 14k silver QA pairs) to enhance agent performance.
rai:machineAnnotationTools: GPT-4o (OpenAI) was used for initial annotation to generate synthetic QA pairs and verify/filter queries. GPT-4 was used as the evaluator to determine correctness of responses by comparing predicted answers with ground truth using CoT prompting. The ai4crawl tool was used to get web pages in Markdown-like format. Beautiful Soup was used to extract clickable HTML buttons and corresponding URLs.
